SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: Civilization Developer Firaxis Lays Off A Third Of Its Staff
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary: Firaxis, the studio behind the Civilization series, has laid off around 60 employees, representing a third of its staff. The report comes from Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier.In a statement provided to Bloomberg by a spokesperson from 2K, a subsidiary of Firaxis' owner, Take-Two, “Firaxis is restructuring and recentering around the studio’s core strength—designing world class strategy games that have set the industry standard for the genre for the last 30 years. As part of these changes, the size of the studio is being reduced to focus on design, technology and the player experience, which means saying goodbye to talented colleagues who helped build Firaxis. These decisions are never easy, but they’re essential to build the next chapter of Firaxis.”In addition to the 60 affected staffers, Firaxis studio head Heather Hazen is also departing. Bloomberg also reports, via anonymous Firaxis employees speaking to the outlet, that the studio is working on an unannounced XCOM game that has had a challenging development, with the team recently missing an important development milestone. This project, if it releases, will be the first Firaxis-developed XCOM game since XCOM: Chimera Squad in 2020.Firaxis’ most recent release is Civilization VII, which launched in February 2025 to favorable reviews but initially "slow" sales, according to Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick last August.  The game currently has a Mixed reception on Steam after Firaxis spent the last year updating the game to address player complaints. Before Civilization VII, Firaxis shipped Marvel's Midnight Suns in 2022, another critically well-received game that failed to meet sales expectations. [Source: Bloomberg]

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: The Blood Of Dawnwalker Just Got A Free 1.2 Update, Adding New Game Plus
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary: The Blood of Dawnwalker is one of the year's biggest, most ambitious games, and the developers over at Rebel Wolves have done a good job cleaning up bugs and performance issues in the weeks since launch. Today, that trend continued; the new 1.2 update is out now on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC, and it adds New Game Plus. The new mode is uniquely ideal for a game like Dawnwalker. The narrative is very player-driven, whether it has to do with your literal dialogue options, your ability to manage your vampiric hunger, or the order you complete quests, and all of these elements can cause your experience to vary wildly. It makes sense, then, that players would want to jump back in to try things again and see what might happen if the game is played differently, and New Game Plus allows them to do that while keeping combat fresh.According to the update notes on the Dawnwalker website, "NG+ unlocks after you complete the game’s Epilogue and lets you experience the story again while keeping your progress – mainly your character level, skills, and inventory." You don't gain access to these skills until you complete the prologue, however, which marks the adventure's proper start.The new mode will also rebalance the world's level scaling. In the base game, certain areas are much harder than others, but in New Game Plus, all enemies will rise in power to match your level, meaning you can explore the world in whatever order you want. On that note, the level cap has also been raised to 100, and protagonist Coen can collect new, more powerful versions of weapons marked with an "NG+" label.That's basically everything in this update. Rebel Wolves also added some slight tweaks to combat in the base game and adjusted some geometry in the open world, but the main focus here was New Game Plus. This is in contrast to the 1.1 update, which added a much wider suite of bug fixes and made the game run more smoothly.

The Blood of Dawnwalker is one of the year's biggest, most ambitious games, and the developers over at Rebel Wolves have done a good job cleaning up bugs and performance issues in the weeks since launch. Today, that trend continued; the new 1.2 update is out now on PS5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC, and it adds New Game Plus.

The new mode is uniquely ideal for a game like Dawnwalker. The narrative is very player-driven, whether it has to do with your literal dialogue options, your ability to manage your vampiric hunger, or the order you complete quests, and all of these elements can cause your experience to vary wildly. It makes sense, then, that players would want to jump back in to try things again and see what might happen if the game is played differently, and New Game Plus allows them to do that while keeping combat fresh.

According to the update notes on the Dawnwalker website, "NG+ unlocks after you complete the game’s Epilogue and lets you experience the story again while keeping your progress – mainly your character level, skills, and inventory." You don't gain access to these skills until you complete the prologue, however, which marks the adventure's proper start.

The new mode will also rebalance the world's level scaling. In the base game, certain areas are much harder than others, but in New Game Plus, all enemies will rise in power to match your level, meaning you can explore the world in whatever order you want. On that note, the level cap has also been raised to 100, and protagonist Coen can collect new, more powerful versions of weapons marked with an "NG+" label.

That's basically everything in this update. Rebel Wolves also added some slight tweaks to combat in the base game and adjusted some geometry in the open world, but the main focus here was New Game Plus. This is in contrast to the 1.1 update, which added a much wider suite of bug fixes and made the game run more smoothly.

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: Star Wars: Galactic Racer Gets Local Splitscreen Multiplayer Next Year
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary:
Star Wars: Galactic Racer has been one of 2026’s breakout titles, but much of the game’s praise stems from its exceptional roguelike single-player mode. If you want to race against human players, you can only do so online. Thankfully, for fans of couch multiplayer, that’s going to change.Developer Fuse Games announced yesterday that local splitscreen multiplayer is coming to Star Wars: Galactic Racer early next year. The mode lets you race up to three other players on the same screen. That's pretty much all there is to it, but given that local multiplayer was the game's biggest omission and, as a result, the most requested addition, there's probably no better news for Galactic Racer fans.We’ve heard you! Local split-screen multiplayer racing is coming in early 2027.

A dedicated team at Fuse Games has been working hard to develop a new mode: Free Play.

Choose your vehicle, character, planet, and track to race alone or with up to 3 other players in local splitscreen action.[image or embed]— STAR WARS: Galactic Racer™ (@starwarsgracer.bsky.social) November 16, 2026 at 11:15 AMStar Wars: Galactic Racer is available now on PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and PC. Read our review of the game here.

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: Make Room For GTAVI By Deleting Your PS5 Trophy Clips
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary: Hard drive space is a premium commodity, and its value has never been more apparent than in the approximately two and a half days leading up to the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. The game is a whopping 209 GB, but thankfully you can purchase the game and preload it now – which you should do because who knows if the servers are going to be able to handle the strain of what is officially the most pre-ordered game ever on both PlayStation and Xbox platforms.The easy (and likely necessary) answer is to delete the big games you aren't currently playing off your hard drive, but there is a cache of arguably unnecessary data on PlayStation 5 that might get you there before you have to make hard decisions.You may have turned it off (Settings > Capture and Broadcasts > Captures > Trophies under the Auto-captures section > Save Trophy Videos under the Video Clips section > Change to None), which if that is the case, then I'm sorry. I can't help you. But the default setting which maybe you've never touched, is saving a lot of unnecessary video.Every time you get a Trophy on PlayStation 5, it creates a short video clip that I bet you never have and never will watch. Here's how to delete all those videos fairly quickly to free up at least some space.First up, go to the Media Gallery. The quickest way to do that is to press the screenshot button to the left of the touchpad, tap over to the most recent media capture on the left, press X, and then press the Go to Media Gallery button. Next, go to the Trophies tab, go to the Sort and Filter option (the downward arrow with the three lines), and change Media Type to Video Clips. After that, go back a few screens and go to the Select Multiple option (the overlapping squares with the check mark on it). Go ahead and press the Select All option, then press Delete, and then hold your breath and commit by pressing Delete again. In taking screenshots to write this little article, I deleted 110 14-second clips. That's about 25 minutes of video footage, which ain't nothing. Maybe it will help you not delete that one game that you started three years ago that you are definitely going to get back to any day now.
SteamGlobalNewsA.HtmlDescription:
Hard drive space is a premium commodity, and its value has never been more apparent than in the approximately two and a half days leading up to the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI. The game is a whopping 209 GB, but thankfully you can purchase the game and preload it now – which you should do because who knows if the servers are going to be able to handle the strain of what is officially the most pre-ordered game ever on both PlayStation and Xbox platforms.

The easy (and likely necessary) answer is to delete the big games you aren't currently playing off your hard drive, but there is a cache of arguably unnecessary data on PlayStation 5 that might get you there before you have to make hard decisions.

You may have turned it off (Settings > Capture and Broadcasts > Captures > Trophies under the Auto-captures section > Save Trophy Videos under the Video Clips section > Change to None), which if that is the case, then I'm sorry. I can't help you. But the default setting which maybe you've never touched, is saving a lot of unnecessary video.

Every time you get a Trophy on PlayStation 5, it creates a short video clip that I bet you never have and never will watch. Here's how to delete all those videos fairly quickly to free up at least some space.

First up, go to the Media Gallery. The quickest way to do that is to press the screenshot button to the left of the touchpad, tap over to the most recent media capture on the left, press X, and then press the Go to Media Gallery button.

Next, go to the Trophies tab, go to the Sort and Filter option (the downward arrow with the three lines), and change Media Type to Video Clips.

After that, go back a few screens and go to the Select Multiple option (the overlapping squares with the check mark on it). Go ahead and press the Select All option, then press Delete, and then hold your breath and commit by pressing Delete again.

In taking screenshots to write this little article, I deleted 110 14-second clips. That's about 25 minutes of video footage, which ain't nothing. Maybe it will help you not delete that one game that you started three years ago that you are definitely going to get back to any day now.

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: 2027 Video Game Grammy Nominations Include Avatar: Frontiers Of Pandora For The Third Time
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary:
Since 2023, the Recording Academy has included an official category for video game soundtracks, adding an air of legitimacy to a diverse musical medium we know and love. Today, we learned the list of nominees for the 2027 Grammy ceremony, and it's an interesting lineup. The nominations are as follows:007: First Light (composed by Joe Henson and Alexis Smith, also known as The Flight)Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora – From the Ashes (composed by John Paesano)Ghost of Yōtei (composed by Toma Otowa)Marvel's Wolverine (composed by David Fleming)Star Wars Zero Company (composed by Gordy Haab)As is often the case, what stands out most about these nominees is how, generally speaking, they don't fully align with gaming culture's favorite soundtracks of the year, and instead often trend toward the most recognizable IP (often franchises with films) of the year. On that note, it's most surprising to see that Avatar: Frontiers of Pandora has been nominated for the third year in a row: once for the base game, once for the Secrets of the Spires DLC, and now for the From The Ashes DLC. None of these soundtracks are bad by any means, but their Grammy representation far outweighs their cultural footprint. 





  
          
                  
              
              
                  

  


  
  
      Ghost of Yōtei
  


The standout here is Ghost of Yōtei, which is not an adaptation of the massive franchises the other games fall into. However, it's also a Sony-published game, which have a pretty good track record of getting nominations, potentially due to the company's massive presence in the music and film industries. Still, Ghost of Yōtei has a great, unique score that's deserving of its spot, and also one previously nominated for best music at the 2025 Game Awards. The Grammys accept any releases between October 1 of one year and September 30 of the following year, so Ghost of Yōtei barely made the cut for this window. The Game Awards nominees will be announced tomorrow – it will be interesting to see how much overlap there is between the categories.This batch of Grammy noms also has fewer recurring nominees than past years. This is Gordy Haab's third nomination (he won in 2024 for Star Wars Jedi: Survivor) and John Paesano's second nomination (he was nominated in 2025 for Marvel's Spider-Man 2). It's also the first year since the awards' creation without Bear McCreary or Austin Wintory nominations.Last year's nominations left a sour taste in the mouths of many, with several DLC nominees and a complete lack of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33, the year's standout hit that many specifically praised for its music. This year certainly has snubs (Mewgenics, Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, and Control Resonant all come to mind), but none as egregious as last year.What do you think was the best video game score from the last year? Let us know in the comments!

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: Cleanser Man Is Mega Man: Dual Override’s Boss Design Contest Winner
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary:
Mega Man: Dual Override’s 2025 reveal brought back the classic boss design contest, asking fans to create and submit their own robot masters, with Capcom choosing one to include in the game. After thousands of submissions, we have our winner; meet Cleanser Man.As his name suggests, Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot who attacks (and tidies) using a long, multi-cleaning hose arm. Capcom has provided the following character summary:Cleanser Man is a cleaning robot with an obsession for pristine beauty. Fueled by an extremely sensitive dirt sensor, Cleaner Man’s ideal world is one without a speck of dust. However, his devotion to cleanliness has a cost. His aggressive scrubbing causes great damage to global landmarks and historic works of art. This fixation has caused the public to view him as more of a threat than a helping hand. Furious and feeling misunderstood, Cleanser Man seizes control of trash processing facility and uses it to pollute the environment with hopes of forcing the world to appreciate the importance of cleanliness.

SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary:
Today is Friday the 13th, but let's not dwell on that. Here are some weekend video games to play. Well, actually, here are some of our biggest stories of the week, and then you can check out some weekend game recommendations.Also, go ahead and make some space on your Xbox or PlayStation hard drive to make room for GTAVI. It's going to be about 200 GB and you can pre-load it now. Delete those games you're not going to return to. Delete all those video clips you'll never watch from every time you get a Trophy on your PlayStation. And you know what? Go ahead and delete Fortnite, too. It's time.Wolfenstein 3 Is Officially In ProductionGrand Theft Auto VI Will Run At 30 FPS On All Consoles, But PS5 Pro Will Feature 'Improved Clarity' And Ray-Traced ShadowsGod Of War Sons Of Sparta Gets PS4 Version And New Content Next MondayThe Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Is Nintendo's Fastest-Selling Switch 2 Game EverMarvel 1943: Rise Of Hydra Reportedly Still In Development Amid Rumors Of Its CancellationSurprising Literally Nobody, Grand Theft Auto VI Is The Most Pre-Ordered Game In PlayStation And Xbox Store History  
  	
				
							
              



      
												
            Funeral For The Sun
      
													
            Marcus Stewart
      
													
            Calling all sickos of The Rootrees Are Dead, Return of the Obra Dinn, The Incident At Galley House, and everything in between: there’s another good deduction game to obsess over. Funeral for the Sun stars a historian who visits an abandoned Latin American town to piece together its turbulent history, chiefly the truth behind the mysterious disappearance of its hundreds of residents (who were, officially speaking, lost in a fire). Supernatural forces allow players to peer into the town’s past to learn about key people potentially responsible for the calamity, who they must identify by name, establish relationships between, and even match younger and older versions of themselves. You even keep track of information using a multi-function notebook à la The Roottrees Are Dead. Boasting an enticing story, a beautiful painterly art direction, and a tight runtime at roughly 8-hours (or less if you’re really on a roll), Funeral for the Sun is a mystery worth unraveling if you need a new deduction game to cozy up with.
      
						
			
	
				
							
              



      
												
            Marvel Rivals
      
													
            Matt Miller
      
													
            NetEase has continued to impress with the pace and quality of its regular updates to Marvel Rivals, which continues today with the release of an 11th season for the superhero battler. Right here at launch, the notable addition is he arrival of X-Men hero Nightcrawler, who BAMFs his way into battle as a strategist, equally capable of healing allies and taking out foes with his sword and brimstone bombs. As is almost always the case right at a new hero’s launch, it can be hard to snag him on the roster on opening day to see how he plays, but once you do, I expect you’ll find him a versatile healer who can pretty dramatically shake up the battlefield, especially with his Ultimate, which basically consolidates allies and enemies together in one central clump for a frenzied exchange of blows. Alongside the new batch of seasonal cosmetics and events to dive into, it’s once again a good time to don your hero outfit and take on some matches.
      
						
			
	
				
							
              



      
												
            Pikmin 4 - Nintendo Switch 2 Edition + Dandori Academy
      
													
            Kyle Hilliard
      
													
            Pikmin 4 released on Switch 2 this week (or upgraded to Switch 2 depending on how you look at it), and that's a good thing. Pikmin 4 is the best game in the series and the Switch 2 version is the best version. That's great for those who never finished the game (your save does transfer) or skipped Pikmin 4 when it released in 2023, but if you're looking for an excuse to return to the game and play new content, the Dandori Academy addition is underwhelming. You can read my full thoughts here.
      
						
			
	
				
							
              



      
												
            Metaphor: ReFantazio On Switch 2
      
													
            Kyle Hilliard
      
													
            Metaphor: ReFantazio, originally released in 2024, is a great RPG from the creators of Persona. And the Persona lineage is obvious throughout the full game. You have to pick and choose where and with whom you should be spending your time, all while a big world-saving RPG with a memorable party of characters plays out in the foreground.It released this week for Switch 2 and it’s a game that I think would play well on a handheld device. It’s also just a good RPG to play if you missed it previously.Fun fact: Metaphor: ReFantazio was the game we had lined up to be the next cover when we were temporarily shut down in in 2024. We went to the studio and had a cover drawn up and everything. You can read the full details of the cover story that never was right here.You can also read Game Informer's review of Metaphor: ReFantazio by following the link.
      
						
			
	
				
							
              



      
												
            Grand Theft Auto: Vice City & Vice City Stories
      
													
            Marcus Stewart
      
													
            As we enjoy the final week in a pre-GTA VI world, what better way to gird your loins for next week’s release, so to speak, than by revisiting the last adventures set in Rockstar’s take on Miami? 2002’s Grand Theft Auto: Vice City is a certified classic that, if you’ve never played it, offers nice foundational insight into what Vice City was like in the ’80s (spoiler: it was a lot like Scarface and Miami Vice). Best of all, Vice City is easily available on current platforms with modernized improvements to boot.If you want to go even further back, chronologically speaking, Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories is a prequel set two years before the events of Vice City. Maybe, in some extremely minute way, Vice City Stories lays narrative groundwork for GTA VI. It’s unlikely, but you never know. Originally released for PSP in 2006, Vice City Stories is trickier to play if you don’t own Sony's retired handheld or a PlayStation 2, which it was ported to in 2007. But if you can find the means, there’s no better time to check out this often overlooked chapter of Vice City’s history.
      
						
			
	
				
							
              



      
												
            Slay the Spire II
      
													
            Charles Harte
      
													
            I usually hold off on early access games, to preserve my experience for the finished product, but I just couldn’t resist Slay the Spire 2. The co-op gameplay is an awesome, major change, but even just adding a couple of new characters and cards would have satisfied my cravings. To that end, this week’s free update adds a brand new character, the Fool, who I’m eager to test out.FYI, this new character is only available on the game’s beta, so you’ll have to go into the game settings on steam, click Properties, then Game Versions & Betas, and then opt into the “public-beta” version of the game to check the new content out. The patch notes for this update specifically say, “We expect to make a great number of content and balance changes before the Fool is ready for the main branch,” so expect frequent tweaks and a bit of a wait before the Fool joins the main Early Access branch. The new beta update also adds two more game modes: Dread and Blitz, which drastically alter your runs. If you want to wait a little while, the team at Mega Crit will refine these options into a more final form. But if you’re like me, more Slay the Spire 2 is more Slay the Spire 2, and I’m hopping in as soon as I can.
      
						
			
	
				
							
              



      
												
            Monster Train 2
      
													
            Charles Harte
      
													
            Monster Train 2 was one of my favorite games of last year, so I’m always glad to have a reason to jump back in. This week’s DLC, The Punished, is a perfect opportunity to do so, adding a new clan to the base game’s already packed roster. Since any clan can be combined with a second one to start a run, adding just one more option at the game’s start has an exponential effect, expanding the ways you can approach each attempt. As the DLC’s name implies, the new Punished clan gains buffs when taking damage, and you get new suite of cards that damages the whole playing field at once, harming foes and bolstering your allies. Even if you’re not checking out the DLC, the base game is absolutely worth picking up – just read my glowing review.
      
						
			
	
				
							
              



      
												
            Tabletop Pick - Cypher Character Rulebook
      
													
            Matt Miller
      
													
            If you’ve been hankering for a new direction to go with your tabletop RPG group, may I recommend the incredibly versatile Cypher System from Monte Cook Games? The new Character Rulebook includes everything you need to get started, and set your adventures in virtually any fictional backdrop you can imagine, from hard sci-fi to gritty horror to high fantasy. Cypher’s polished approach to narrative-first and player-focused game sessions is much easier to pick up than many new rules systems, but it has enormous flexibility to deliver smart, creative, and exciting adventures that can help to change things up if your playing group has been in a rut.

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: God Of War Sons Of Sparta Gets PS4 Version And New Content Next Monday
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary: It's been about nine months since Sony Santa Monica and Mega Cat Studios dropped God of War Sons of Sparta as a surprise reveal and launch during a State of Play. If you haven't checked it out yet, the developers are giving you some new reasons to today, unveiling two new modes and a new platform: PlayStation 4.If you don't remember, God of War Sons of Sparta is a prequel spin-off of the God of War series, showing protagonist Kratos as a 13-year-old soldier, long before his god-killing days. The game features 2D combat and a Metroidvania-style map, along with a fully voiced cast of characters including Scott Menville (who you might recognize as Robin in Teen Titans) as Kratos' brother Deimos, Jack Quaid (who will voice a different character in God of War Laufey next year), and TC Carson, who returns from the original trilogy as the voice of adult Kratos.Announced in a post on the PlayStation Blog today, Sons of Sparta is making the jump back to Sony's previous console, which is now (brace yourself) 13 years old. Sons of Sparta's 2D pixel art is far less demanding than the other God of War entries, though, so it's no surprise this was possible – it's mainly surprising that they're doing it at all.  For PS5 players who already own the game, developer Mega Cat is also adding two new modes: Hermes Mode and Erebus Mode. Hermes Mode, named after the Greek god of wind, mail, and speed, is a speedrun mode that encourages you to beat the game as quickly as possible, complete with a split-based timer in the upper right-hand corner of the screen. Meanwhile, Erebus Mode, named after one of the domains of the underworld (you'll be familiar with it if you've played the Hades games), makes the game far deadlier as Kratos and all his foes die in a single hit. You'll have to wait until you beat the game once to unlock Erebus Mode, but you can access Hermes Mode from a fresh save by entering the following (and semi-familiar) code in the start menu: Up, Up, Down, Down, Left, Right, Left, Right, L1, R1, Touchpad.The free update and PS4 version will be available next Monday, November 16, at midnight local time. For more Sons of Sparta, check out our review. For more God of War, bad news: God of War Laufey was just delayed until May.

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: Wolfenstein 3 Is Officially In Production
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary:
Wolfenstein 3 is officially underway at MachineGames, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has announced. The announcement of the third mainline Wolfenstein title in MachineGames’ trilogy comes over seven years after the launch of the fourth and most recent spin-off entry, Wolfenstein: Youngblood. Sharma’s announcement includes a teaser image of the script for Wolfenstein 3's first chapter. MachineGames echoed this reveal with its own post, which includes a photo of a motion capture session featuring actress Debra Wilson, who plays Grace Walker in the series.Wolfenstein 3 is officially in production at @MachineGames. One of gaming's most important franchises, and a team that has done remarkable work bringing it forward. Looking forward to sharing more. https://t.co/YyX8LrbTvh— ASHA (@asha_shar) November 12, 2026
MachineGames’ last release was 2024’s well-received Indiana Jones and the Great Circle, but studio co-founder Jerk Gustafsson stated in a NoClip documentary last year that he hoped to finish BJ Blazkowicz’s story. Based on Gustafsson’s comment, it sounds like Wolfenstein 3 very recently started production, so we probably shouldn’t expect any substantial update for a good while. This won’t be the only new Wolfenstein project, as Amazon is developing a live-action series based on the franchise. Until either the new game or the show releases, you can tide yourself over by reading our reviews of Wolfenstein: The New Order, Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus, and Wolfenstein: Youngblood.

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: Halo: Campaign Evolved Gets Firefight Mode In Free Update This Winter
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary:
Halo: Campaign Evolved is getting the fan-favorite Firefight mode via a free update this winter, an Xbox Wire post announces. The update will allow players to team up in cooperative wave-based PvE.Firefight, which debuted in Halo 3: ODST, lets up to four players team up to survive waves of enemies. The mode has become a popular staple and has appeared in multiple Halo games, but this will be the first time that it has been retroactively added to the original entry. 





  
      
      

  
    

  
      
            


      
  



    
  
  
  


Xbox FanFest attendees, a global multi-city event, will be the first to go hands-on with Campaign Evolved’s take on Firefight. Additionally, more details about Firefight will be shared during Halo Fest in Seattle on December 12-13, where the mode will also be playable for attendees.You can read our review of Halo: Campaign Evolved here. Subscribers can also learn about the game's development by reading our cover story from this summer. Be sure to also read the recent Halo news that Microsoft is handing the franchise to Activision after gutting long-time developer Halo Studios.

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: Marvel 1943: Rise Of Hydra Reportedly Still In Development Amid Rumors Of Its Cancellation
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary:
Yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, new reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.The rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was quickly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.  Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance New Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate. However, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. However, Schreier adds this could change due to the uncertainty caused by the recent merger between Warner Bros. Yesterday, a rumor emerged on X claiming that Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra, the upcoming World War II-era superhero game led by Uncharted creator Amy Hennig, was being cancelled. After making the rounds on social media, new reports claim this is not the case, at least for now.

The rumor stemmed from a now-deleted X post from a fan account called Marvel 1943 Rise Of Hydra Countdown claiming, through supposed inside sources, that Skydance was preparing to announce the game’s cancellation. This rumor was quickly picked up and circulated by online gaming circles, gaining steam due to growing uncertainty around the game’s status.  

Marvel 1943: Rise of Hydra was revealed in 2022 and stars Captain America and Black Panther (Azurri, T'Challa's grandfather), alongside Howling Commandos member Gabriel Jones and Wakandan Spy Network leader Nanali, as they battle Hydra during World War II. Developed by Skydance New Media, led by Amy Hennig, it’s been repeatedly delayed, and only cinematic footage has been released. This has understandably caused many to question the game’s fate.

However, a few hours after the cancellation rumor made the rounds, Bloomberg’s Jason Schreier reported on Bluesky that Skydance’s leadership addressed the rumor with the development team on Slack and assured them Marvel 1943 was not canceled. Discovery and Paramount Skydance (Skydance New Media is a game development branch of the now-merged Skydance Corporation).

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Remake Is Nintendo's Fastest-Selling Switch 2 Game Ever
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Nintendo's second remake of the original N64 game that first launched way back in 1998, is the fastest-selling Nintendo-published game on the Switch 2 ever. That accolade comes after the game sold more than 5.2 million copies in just four days following its November 5 launch last week. This remake is already the Switch 2's second-best-selling Nintendo game at 5.2 million units sold, behind Mario Kart World's impressive 16.48 million copies sold to date. If The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time keeps this pace up, it could one day overtake Mario Kart World, though the Mario Kart series typically holds onto that top spot. Mario Kart 8 Deluxe is still far and away the best-selling game on Switch.  The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time is the crown jewel of Nintendo's 40th Zelda series anniversary celebration, which also includes other games, products, and even an upcoming worldwide orchestral tour. Plus, a live-action Legend of Zelda film will debut in theaters worldwide on April 30, 2027. Game Informer gave The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time a 9.25 out of 10 in its review, with our reviewer Kyle Hilliard writing, "For many like me, the original Ocarina of Time is an impactful adventure that arrived at a time in their lives when magic still felt real. Playing the game 28 years later and appreciating the care taken to maintain and improve the original vision was the ultimate surprise of the whole experience: I didn't expect to be so moved." The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time launched last week exclusively on Nintendo Switch 2. For more, read this interview with the remake's producers about changes to the original game, easter eggs, the Bombchu bowling alley operator, and more, then check out this feature breaking down the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time easter eggs that did and didn't make it into this 2026 remake. After that, read about how the Switch 2 Pro controller can make The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time even better, then check out this interview with award-winning composer and musician Jon Batiste about the Ocarina of Time score. Did you pick up The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time last week? Let us know what you think of it so far in the comments below!

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: PlayStation Cancels In-Development Live-Service Shooter, Fairgames, At Jade Raymond's Former Haven Studio
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary: PlayStation has reportedly canceled Fairgames, the long-in-development live-service shooter being made by Haven Studios, which Jade Raymond founded in 2021. Sony acquired Haven in 2022, and in 2025, Raymond left the studio, though it remained dedicated to developing Fairgames without her. It seems the story of Fairgames is now over, according to a new Bloomberg report.The publication reports that PlayStation will not enforce any job cuts or layoffs as a result of Fairgames' cancellation, which comes as a surprise, and the studio will instead shift to support other first-party teams under the PlayStation umbrella. According to Bloomberg, this cancellation comes after a recent test of the game that allowed "thousands of players" to check it out did not deliver the results PlayStation wanted.  "While the test demonstrated strong operational excellence, live ops readiness and community engagement, player feedback and retention results were mixed and fell short of the goals we had set," PlayStation executives Sean Decker and John Doyle wrote in an email to employees today, according to Bloomberg. "Combined with challenging market conditions in the PVP shooter genre, we have made the difficult decision to cease development on the game." This doesn't necessarily come as a surprise. PlayStation announced Fairgames back in 2023 and hasn't shown much since, leaving many to assume development has been struggling behind the scenes. Since then, PlayStation has pulled back heavily on its live-service plans, which originally included launching more than 10 live-service games by March of this year. Naughty Dog's Last of Us multiplayer game was canceled, Bungie ended active development on Destiny 2, and live-service Horizon spin-off Hunters Gathering is reportedly being overhauled following poor playtest feedback, amongst other stories. Reading between the lines, many fans were waiting for news like today's cancellation of Fairgames to drop. Still, in an era where games are canceled and entire teams are laid off (sometimes even after releasing a successful game), it's nice to see Haven employees are not facing layoffs. [Source: Bloomberg]

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: Bandai Namco Shuts Down Unknown 9: Awakening Developer Reflector Entertainment
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary: Bandai Namco has announced it is shutting down Reflector Entertainment, the Montreal studio behind 2024’s Unknown 9: Awakening. Reflector, founded in 2015, is a subsidiary of Bandai Namco that was acquired in 2020. Unknown 9: Awakening is the studio’s only released title, which was first revealed at Gamescom 2020 and released on October 17, 2024. The third-person action game is set within the broader Unknown 9 transmedia franchise, which includes a book trilogy, comics, and a web series, and stars Haroona, a woman able to traverse a separate dimension called the Fold. Haroona, played by The Witcher actress Anya Chalotra, uses this ability and other supernatural powers to battle a hostile secret society across India and other global locations. Upon release, Unknown 9: Awakening didn’t make much of a critical splash; it currently has a 59 Metascore and "Mixed" Steam reviews. In November 2024, a month after Unknown 9's launch, Reflector laid off 18 percent of its staff.  More layoffs were announced in January 2025 as Reflector canned an unannounced project while confirming Unknown 9 failed to meet expectations. With Reflector’s dissolution, Bandai Namco expects to post “an extraordinary loss” of approximately €21 million on its Q3 financial results for the fiscal year ending March 31, 2027.

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: Surprising Literally Nobody, Grand Theft Auto VI Is The Most Pre-Ordered Game In PlayStation And Xbox Store History
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary: Grand Theft Auto VI launches next week on Thursday, November 19. You can preload the game on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S starting today, as detailed by Rockstar Games, PlayStation, and Xbox. Alongside this announcement, both PlayStation and Xbox have revealed that – surprise! – GTA VI is the most preordered game in the history of their respective digital stores. That's not shocking – GTA VI is, by many metrics, the most anticipated game in history, with its predecessor, Grand Theft Auto V, selling nearly 235 million copies since its launch back in 2013. There's also the fact that Rockstar Games is not releasing a physical edition of GTA VI, per se. Yes, you can go to a store to pick up a GTA VI box (and you can do so today, allowing you to preload the game), but inside that box will be a download code for a digital version of the game – you won't find GTA VI on a physical disc. So, naturally, many players are opting to purchase the game on digital storefronts like the PlayStation and Xbox game stores.  "Grand Theft Auto VI, the most preordered title of all time on the Microsoft Store, launches November 19," an Xbox blog post reads. "Considering the unprecedented demand, we encourage everyone to begin preloading as soon as possible to ensure you're prepared for launch day." PlayStation echoes this statement with a blog post of its own that reads, "Grand Theft Auto VI is now the most preordered game in the history of the PlayStation Store. Given this unprecedented demand, we've joined with Rockstar Games to allow players to start preloading the game nine days early, so they're ready to play on launch day." There you have it: People are very excited about Grand Theft Auto VI. Grand Theft Auto VI launches next week on November 19 on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. For more, check out the song "Pusher" from the game's original score, then check out the GTA VI launch trailer. After that, check out this exclusive story about how GTA VI features over 170 animal species and another about its tropical storms and hurricanes. Be sure to read about how GTA VI will target 30 FPS gameplay on all consoles, too.

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: Marathon’s Symbiosis Update Adds Host Of New Modes, Including Permanent PvE, Next Month
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary: Bungie has detailed its upcoming Symbiosis update for Marathon, which introduces several significant modes next month. Chief among them is the new permanent PvE mode, which Bungie previously experimented with and promised earlier this year. Symbiosis is headlined by Expedition, a co-op PvE destination with roguelite elements. Expedition pits teams of players against escalating challenges and offers randomized upgrades called Flash Boosts to increase their odds of success. The Perimeter zone has also been expanded with the new Burrows and Reservoir areas. Another addition is Limbo, a new social hub for players to gather that features a firing range. You can also try out the new sword-wielding Bishop Runner Shell alongside new weapons and gear, such as the Maverick pistol, throwing knife, hack grenade, and V17 flamethrower. Lastly, you can test your skills against other players in the beta PvP Deathmatch mode.  Symbiosis arrives in Marathon on December 8. An open play week will kick off the same day, allowing new players to experience all of Marathon’s content for free until December 15. The Symbiosis update marks Marathon's evolution into a more co-op-friendly, PvE experience as its initial focus on PvP extraction has struggled to sustain a substantial audience since its March 5 launch. Bungie announced in September that it plans to spend the rest of 2026 improving Marathon's core mechanics and features while giving players more agency for how they engage with it beyond competitive PvP. For more on Marathon, check out our review.

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: House House Discloses AI Use For 'Under 0.1%' Of Big Walk's Code Following IGF Voting Controversy
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary: Big Walk developer House House has found itself at the center of a controversy over the upcoming Independent Games Festival on March 3, 2027, after a group of its jurors said they would not vote for any game that has used generative AI in any capacity. The jurors' statement does not name House House or Big Walk, but the studio eventually updated its FAQ to explain how it used generative AI for coding after IGF discussions. After vaguely posting on social media, those associated with IGF made clear that a sticking point in the voting process was Big Walk.Former games journalist and game developer Austin Walker posted the IGF jurors' statement on Bluesky, explaining that voting has been difficult this year due to the "significant increase in the number of submitted games developed with generative AI tools.""This has set off some fairly intense discussion and disagreement across the judge and jury pools, and at this point there is no universal consensus on what (if anything) is to be done," the statement reads. "The IGF has affirmed that we may cast our votes according to our own tastes and values. But we, as a contingent of IGF jurors, feel that this trend and the games embracing it deserve stronger pushback than a vote in silence."  The statement continues, explaining that not all jurors are on board with the blanket statement, citing reasons including "their ability to safely sign without professional blowback." It continues, "Above all: Our goal is to state solidarity with those who despair over the future of their art, their craft, and their industry – including those who have experimented with these tools, but who now believe they are not in our best interest." The statement continues with the jurors' beliefs regarding gen-AI, including its negative effects, that any gen-AI used in any process of game development is not okay, noting specifically that "AI-generated code is not an exception to these harms," and more. "For those reasons, this year we are declining to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity," the statement says. "We urge the IGF to adopt a strong anti-AI policy for future years that disallows games containing any AI-generated work." The statement then includes the names of the IGF jurors who signed it. Big Walk isn't specifically mentioned within that statement. However, Kyle LeClair, a four-time IGF judge and a juror for the upcoming IGF, tells Aftermath that "it got to the point where the most-discussed game this year almost entirely involved its AI usage, overshadowing pretty much everything else." LeClair says it felt like a boiling point, adding, "Anyhow, strong props to the jurors for taking this stance and putting out this letter as well, even if some people believe that using AI for coding purposes is a more gray area, we're at a point where the amount of AI slop clogging up the indie game scene means having to take hard stances such as this in order to discourage such an amount of recklessness."  Again, no mention of Big Walk. However, game developer Bruno Diaz took to BlueSky to confirm the speculation: that most-discussed game was Big Walk. "Okay, because the cat is out of the f---ing bag, I might as well combat misinformation a bit: 1. The reason IGF judges are aware of the LLM use in the development of Big Walk is through a disclosure shared by House House. 2. This disclosure was required by IGF rules. 3. While some have characterized the LLM usage as just fixing one individual blocking bug, this is a bit inaccurate; the description given by House House mentioned there being several instances, though they did also say it was mostly 'consultative' use and not code gen or agents."Diaz notes that they believe that distinction is without a difference, adding that "to my knowledge, it is not the case that Big Walk is non-compliant with the former [Steam's AI disclosure requirements]." "Yes, there was a large discussion about this in internal IGF forums," Diaz said. "Yes, a lot of people said things that I personally think were disingenuous, extremely disappointing, or just (frankly) dumb. No, I have no intention of talking about it in further detail or exposing anyone. [...] Ultimately, it is extremely difficult for a group of over 100 people to keep a secret so I expected this to come out eventually. Shrug emoji. If you think something is reputationally damaging, consider not doing it."  With discussion surrounding Big Walk happening during the IGF discussions, House House updated its FAQ to address, "Was AI used to make Big Walk?" Here's what the FAQ reads, in full: "In the final stretch of Big Walk’s development, LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs. In some cases, snippets from LLM responses were copied as a starting point to be modified into game code—we’d estimate that well under 0.1% of Big Walk’s code had anything to do with this usage, and generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game.The primary use case for House House’s use of LLMs was to research, via chatbots, issues we encountered with third-party code. If you’re technically-minded, and curious, here’s an example. We needed to cull shadow casters by distance from the camera, but Unity URP only allows culling shadow casters by distance in camera forwards, so shadow casters behind the player were being rendered at an infinite distance. This made our game run 50% slower for around 20 seconds at sunrise and sunset. We researched the problem extensively, and we looked at the URP code ourselves, but we couldn’t find a way. Then, we were able to speak directly to an engineer at Unity, who asked around and ultimately concluded that what we wanted wasn’t possible. Finally, we posed the question to an LLM chatbot. After a few dead ends, it suggested a possible fix, and while we had to modify the suggestion extensively, it worked. This fix represented about 10 lines of code inside URP.We originally wrote a version of the above disclosure as it was a suggested part of our IGF submission. We have not made any disclosure on Steam as the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage. We are posting this disclosure as it has become a matter of public interest.This is not an endorsement of, or argument for, the use of AI tools, however minimal. We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as “inevitable”. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologise that Big Walk’s LLM usage may not meet their standards.Big Walk was developed without an internal AI usage policy in place, and we consider that lack of policy a failure. We will work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards."As you can see, House House did not disclose its use of AI-generated code because "Steam as a platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage." It says it is posting the disclosure now as "it has become a matter of public interest." House House recently made headlines for choosing not to put Big Walk on Xbox in accordance with the Palestinian-led BDS boycott against Microsoft Games. Earlier this year, it gained widespread critical acclaim for its unique emphasis on cooperative puzzle-solving – you can read more about that in Game Informer's Big Walk review.

It continues, "Above all: Our goal is to state solidarity with those who despair over the future of their art, their craft, and their industry – including those who have experimented with these tools, but who now believe they are not in our best interest." 

The statement continues with the jurors' beliefs regarding gen-AI, including its negative effects, that any gen-AI used in any process of game development is not okay, noting specifically that "AI-generated code is not an exception to these harms," and more. 

"For those reasons, this year we are declining to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity," the statement says. "We urge the IGF to adopt a strong anti-AI policy for future years that disallows games containing any AI-generated work." The statement then includes the names of the IGF jurors who signed it. 

Big Walk isn't specifically mentioned within that statement. However, Kyle LeClair, a four-time IGF judge and a juror for the upcoming IGF, tells Aftermath that "it got to the point where the most-discussed game this year almost entirely involved its AI usage, overshadowing pretty much everything else." LeClair says it felt like a boiling point, adding, "Anyhow, strong props to the jurors for taking this stance and putting out this letter as well, even if some people believe that using AI for coding purposes is a more gray area, we're at a point where the amount of AI slop clogging up the indie game scene means having to take hard stances such as this in order to discourage such an amount of recklessness." 

Again, no mention of Big Walk. However, game developer Bruno Diaz took to BlueSky to confirm the speculation: that most-discussed game was Big Walk. "Okay, because the cat is out of the f---ing bag, I might as well combat misinformation a bit: 1. The reason IGF judges are aware of the LLM use in the development of Big Walk is through a disclosure shared by House House. 2. This disclosure was required by IGF rules. 3. While some have characterized the LLM usage as just fixing one individual blocking bug, this is a bit inaccurate; the description given by House House mentioned there being several instances, though they did also say it was mostly 'consultative' use and not code gen or agents."

Diaz notes that they believe that distinction is without a difference, adding that "to my knowledge, it is not the case that Big Walk is non-compliant with the former [Steam's AI disclosure requirements]." 

"Yes, there was a large discussion about this in internal IGF forums," Diaz said. "Yes, a lot of people said things that I personally think were disingenuous, extremely disappointing, or just (frankly) dumb. No, I have no intention of talking about it in further detail or exposing anyone. [...] Ultimately, it is extremely difficult for a group of over 100 people to keep a secret so I expected this to come out eventually. Shrug emoji. If you think something is reputationally damaging, consider not doing it." 

With discussion surrounding Big Walk happening during the IGF discussions, House House updated its FAQ to address, "Was AI used to make Big Walk?" Here's what the FAQ reads, in full: 

"In the final stretch of Big Walk’s development, LLMs were used sparingly by House House to help work through difficult technical challenges and bugs. In some cases, snippets from LLM responses were copied as a starting point to be modified into game code—we’d estimate that well under 0.1% of Big Walk’s code had anything to do with this usage, and generative AI was not used in any other context when making the game.

The primary use case for House House’s use of LLMs was to research, via chatbots, issues we encountered with third-party code. If you’re technically-minded, and curious, here’s an example. We needed to cull shadow casters by distance from the camera, but Unity URP only allows culling shadow casters by distance in camera forwards, so shadow casters behind the player were being rendered at an infinite distance. This made our game run 50% slower for around 20 seconds at sunrise and sunset. We researched the problem extensively, and we looked at the URP code ourselves, but we couldn’t find a way. Then, we were able to speak directly to an engineer at Unity, who asked around and ultimately concluded that what we wanted wasn’t possible. Finally, we posed the question to an LLM chatbot. After a few dead ends, it suggested a possible fix, and while we had to modify the suggestion extensively, it worked. This fix represented about 10 lines of code inside URP.

We originally wrote a version of the above disclosure as it was a suggested part of our IGF submission. We have not made any disclosure on Steam as the platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage. We are posting this disclosure as it has become a matter of public interest.

This is not an endorsement of, or argument for, the use of AI tools, however minimal. We have some concern that voluntary disclosures like this might contribute to the normalisation of this technology, or its treatment as “inevitable”. We support the work of those who are trying to limit the harm generative AI is doing to videogames and our world, and apologise that Big Walk’s LLM usage may not meet their standards.

Big Walk was developed without an internal AI usage policy in place, and we consider that lack of policy a failure. We will work to have a more comprehensive policy going forwards."

As you can see, House House did not disclose its use of AI-generated code because "Steam as a platform does not request disclosure of code or chatbot usage." It says it is posting the disclosure now as "it has become a matter of public interest." 

House House recently made headlines for choosing not to put Big Walk on Xbox in accordance with the Palestinian-led BDS boycott against Microsoft Games. Earlier this year, it gained widespread critical acclaim for its unique emphasis on cooperative puzzle-solving – you can read more about that in Game Informer's Big Walk review.

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: Update: You Can Preload Grand Theft Auto VI On PS5 and Xbox Today, And You Should Because It's Massive
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary: Update, 11/10/26:Rockstar Games revealed last week that players can preload Grand Theft Auto VI on their console of choice the following week, and that time has arrived. The studio released a blog post today to announce that you can preload GTA VI on PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S. If you're excited about the game, you will probably want to go ahead and do this because it will take up a whopping 212 GB of space on your drives – make the room now so you don't hit this roadblock next week when the game goes live on Thursday, November 19. The blog post also details performance on PlayStation and Xbox consoles, and you can read more about what to expect here. The original story continues below...Original story, 11/03/26:We're just over two weeks away from the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, which recently graced the cover of Game Informer. Ahead of its November 19 launch, Rockstar Games has announced that digital preloading for GTA VI will begin next week on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. More specifically, preloading on Xbox Series X/S will begin Tuesday, November 10, at 12 a.m. GMT (4 p.m. PT/7 p.m. ET on November 9), and on PS5 at midnight local time in your time zone. Although Rockstar isn't producing physical discs of GTA VI, you can still buy a physical box at retail, which includes a download code for the game. After that, check out this exclusive story about how GTA VI features over 170 animal species and another about how the game features tropical storms and hurricanes. What are you most excited to experience in Grand Theft Auto VI? Let us know in the comments below!

Update, 11/10/26:

Rockstar Games revealed last week that players can preload Grand Theft Auto VI on their console of choice the following week, and that time has arrived. The studio released a blog post today to announce that you can preload GTA VI on PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S. If you're excited about the game, you will probably want to go ahead and do this because it will take up a whopping 212 GB of space on your drives – make the room now so you don't hit this roadblock next week when the game goes live on Thursday, November 19. 

The blog post also details performance on PlayStation and Xbox consoles, and you can read more about what to expect here. 

The original story continues below...

Original story, 11/03/26:

We're just over two weeks away from the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, which recently graced the cover of Game Informer. Ahead of its November 19 launch, Rockstar Games has announced that digital preloading for GTA VI will begin next week on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S. 

More specifically, preloading on Xbox Series X/S will begin Tuesday, November 10, at 12 a.m. GMT (4 p.m. PT/7 p.m. ET on November 9), and on PS5 at midnight local time in your time zone. Although Rockstar isn't producing physical discs of GTA VI, you can still buy a physical box at retail, which includes a download code for the game. The studio says, "Code-in-box versions for both consoles should be available from retailers beginning November 12." 

The preload file will require 212 GB on your device, so make sure you have the space before you start the download. You can find more details about this process here. 

Elsewhere in today's GTA VI news, Rockstar has revealed that on November 19, it will add an official printable GTA VI cover art poster and a map of Leonida as a free digital download to the game's official site. However, a double-sided physical version of this poster will be made available shortly after the launch of GTA VI from the Rockstar Store. It will only cost $0.99 on its own, or come free with any other purchase from the store. 

GTA VI launches November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. 

For more, check out the song "Pusher" from the game's original score, then check out the GTA VI launch trailer. After that, check out this exclusive story about how GTA VI features over 170 animal species and another about how the game features tropical storms and hurricanes. 

What are you most excited to experience in Grand Theft Auto VI? Let us know in the comments below!

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: Grand Theft Auto VI Will Run At 30 FPS On All Consoles, But PS5 Pro Will Feature 'Improved Clarity' And Ray-Traced Shadows
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary: Grand Theft Auto VI launches next week on Thursday, November 19, and you can preload the game on your PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S starting today, Rockstar Games has announced. The studio has also revealed what kind of visuals players can expect on their respective consoles, making clear that regardless of where you play, GTA VI targets 30 FPS gameplay. "Grand Theft Auto VI has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits to bring the vast and rich world of Leonida to life – while maintaining the density and visual fidelity of all its environments and inhabitants," Rockstar writes in a blog post.  Rockstar Games also breaks down the different graphical settings available on PlayStation and Xbox consoles. On PS5 Pro, GTA VI will feature "improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows only available on PlayStation 5 Pro." On PS5 and PS5 Pro, the game will include "high-fidelity haptic feedback" fully integrated into DualSense controllers and adjustable via accessibility settings, improved spatial rendering so all in-game sounds take full advantage of Tempest 3D audio, and improved load times, "making Grand Theft Auto VI play best on PlayStation 5 consoles." On Xbox consoles, Rockstar doesn't dive into performance; instead, it focuses on Xbox Cloud Gaming on Xbox Series X/S and Xbox One consoles, noting this feature will use Xbox Series S graphics settings. GTA VI will also fully support Remote Play on PlayStation and Xbox. GTA VI launches November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. For more, check out the song "Pusher" from the game's original score, then check out the GTA VI launch trailer. After that, check out this exclusive story about how GTA VI features over 170 animal species and another about its tropical storms and hurricanes. Where will you play GTA VI? Let us know in the comments below!

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – November 6, 2026
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary:
This week and weekend is all about the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, one of the few games I feel deserves the title of masterpiece. And the remake is really well done! I got every heart piece, every Gold Skulltala, the Goron Sword, and the biggest pouch for every one of my items over the course of the review... but I am contemplating jumping right back in for another go.We also revealed our next cover and in case you missed the announcement it is... pause for effect... Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis! It's an awesome cover that celebrates the history of Lara Croft, and along with a cover story on the game, we also have a big retrospective on the series. I highly recommend subscribing to get your issue if you haven't already.But it wasn't all just Zelda and Tomb Raider this week. Below you will find a list of weekend play recommendations, but before that... some of our biggest stories of the week.Cover Reveal – Tomb Raider: Legacy Of AtlantisZelda Ocarina Remake Producers Talk Changing And Maintaining The Game, Easter Eggs, The Bombchu Bowling Alley Operator, And MoreThe Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Easter Eggs That Did And Did Not Make It Into The 2026 RemakeThe Switch 2 Pro Controller Can Make Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Even BetterThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (2026) Review – Exceptionally FamiliarGod Of War Laufey Delayed To May101 Rapid-Fire Questions With Exodus Devs  
  	
				
							
              



      
												
            The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time (2026)
      
													
            Kyle Hilliard
      
													
            We have been writing a lot about The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time remake this week because it is one of 2026's most exciting games, and it's real good. The remake is not particularly surprising. It mostly sticks to the trajectory of the original game, but there is a reason it is considered one of the best games of all time. It also looks and plays amazing. You can read the full review here (or watch the video above), but we also have a big interview with the game's producers (one of whom worked on the original Ocarina of Time, and one who directed Breath of the Wild among many other Zelda games), some details about the Easter Eggs that did and did not make it into the remake, and a very handy tip for the game if you happen to be playing with a Switch 2 Pro controller.
      
						
			
	
				
							
              



      
												
            World Of Warcraft: Forever
      
													
            Alex Van Aken
      
													
            World of Warcraft: Forever is out now and it’s a great time to jump into the revamped and expanded version of a project that changed online games forever back in 2004. A thousand new quests, multiple new zones, countless revamps, and an impressively stunning visual overhaul make it the perfect time to jump in for anyone who’s ever been curious to explore Azeroth.
      
						
			
	
				
							
              



      
												
            Escape Academy 2: Back To School
      
													
            Kyle Hilliard
      
													
            2022's Escape Academy was a sneaky little puzzle game that surprised me and its sequel released this week. Taking place in a school obsessed with puzzles, you play as a student who must make their way through a series of escape rooms. The puzzles are clever, and the setting is charming, but the secret weapon is the local, split-screen co-op. Solving puzzles together is fun especially when one player needs to look at one section of a room to help dictate a solution on the other side of the room. My wife and I both love video games, but rarely play co-op games together just because of our disparate, individual tastes. But Escape Room is one we enjoyed together and we're so far enjoying the sequel. My only complaint so far is... I wish it ran a little better.
      
						
			
	
				
							
              



      
												
            Moadra
      
													
            Matt Miller
      
													
            While we collectively use the term here for the sake of familiarity, I’m always a bit hesitant in my own mind to label a game under the wide banner of “Metroidvania.” In part, that’s because I think the two referenced games (Metroid and Castlevania: Symphony of the Night) are actually more different than they might appear at first glance. Gloomsoft’s recent release, Moadra, recognizes that distinction, crafting a game that draws heavy inspiration from the specific tradition of Super Metroid, even while presenting an intriguing and atmospheric fiction that is great fun to discover. In movement, actions, and exploration, Moadra feels remarkably similar to  the best of the 2D Metroid games. A scanning tool also leans into the Metroid inspirations, revealing details about the weird alien world you’re navigating. If you’ve been hungry for a game that scratches that particular itch of sci-fi gear/ability-gated exploration, I think you’ll find a lot to love in this game.
      
						
			
	
				
							
              



      
												
            Marvel’s Guardians Of The Galaxy: Encore Edition On Switch 2
      
													
            Kyle Hilliard
      
													
            I get the Marvel fatigue we've all been experiencing. There are a lot of games and a lot of movies and a lot of TV shows and many are good, but lately most feel like homework. For those reasons, you'd be forgiven for dismissing the 2021 Guardians of the Galaxy game, but I promise you it is good. For one, it is standalone. It does not directly tie to any specific Marvel media. No homework necessary. And for two, it's just a really good game with an affecting story and a unique take on the characters that most of us met for the first time in the movies. And, for the BioWare fans out there mourning the loss of Mass Effect, this game has some Mass Effect energy. It's available on Switch 2 this week and I happily recommend it, especially if you missed it five years ago. 
      
						
			
	
				
							
              



      
												
            Tabletop Pick – Lairs
      
													
            Matt Miller
      
													
            This exclusively two-player board game features a fun mix of activities. You act as both a dungeon architect, and an adventurer delving into said dungeons. Each player creates their own version of a challenging dungeon filled with traps, monsters, and treasures. 





  
          
                  
              
              
                  

  


  
  
  


But you’re also forced to take on the dangers of your opponent’s crafted dungeon, to see who manages to come out on top. If you have fond memories of the hidden-info nature of old games like Battleship, but you want some greater strategic depth and fantasy flavor thrown in, this one is a great pick.

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: God Of War Laufey Delayed To May
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary: PlayStation first-party developer Santa Monica Studio has delayed its upcoming action game, God of War Laufey, to May. More specifically, the PlayStation 5-exclusive title will now launch on May 20, representing a roughly three-month delay from the original February 16 release date. "Since the reveal of God of War Laufey in June, we've been deeply grateful to see so much excitement for Faye's journey through the Everywhen," a statement from the studio reads. "We don't take for granted the trusted place in the studio to make an extraordinary experience worthy of the passion and dedication of our fans. With this in mind, we've made the decision to delay God of War Laufey's release to May 20, 2027. We will make the most of each moment until then by putting in the finishing touches and pushing the game to its fullest potential. On behalf of everyone on the team, we appreciate your patience and we'll be back to share more updates soon."  God of War Laufey stars Faye, Kratos' deceased wife from his Norse adventures, after she ends up in the mysterious realm known as the Everywhen following her death. There, she will fight monsters and creatures from various mythologies alongside a talking gelatinous cube and a talking sword sash. We'll have to wait a bit longer than expected now to see what her adventure entails. God of War Laufey will now launch on PS5 next year on May 20. In the meantime, check out this newly revealed weapon, then read about how Amazon's God of War TV series has recast Kratos as Dave Bautista.

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: Cover Reveal – Tomb Raider: Legacy Of Atlantis
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary: Game Informer’s next cover story is Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis, the upcoming reimagining of the original 1996 Tomb Raider arriving on February 12. Since that game celebrates the franchise’s 30th anniversary this year, we’re doing the same with a double-whammy of Tomb Raider features. We visited Crystal Dynamics’ office to play Legacy of Atlantis for several hours, including an exclusive tour of the Greece section. For our 12-page cover story, we spoke to key team members at Crystal Dynamics and Flying Wild Hog to learn why it’s tackling Lara Croft’s seminal adventure once again (having already remade the game once in Tomb Raider: Anniversary), how this version of the game differs from previous incarnations and why, discuss the teams' controversial use of AI development tools, and how Legacy of Atlantis plants seeds for the upcoming Tomb Raider: Catalyst.The issue also includes a six-page retrospective of Tomb Raider’s 30-year history, with insights from Crystal Dynamics. This celebration is reflected in our cover art, designed by Tomb Raider franchise art director Brenoch Adams, which showcases every version of Lara Croft from the Core Design, Legend, Survivor, and current eras.  The December issue also marks the return of our annual (and very large) holiday buyers guide, featuring curated gift suggestions for the gamers in your life ahead of the winter holidays. Furthermore, we’ve created a list of family-friendly games to enjoy with younger relatives during upcoming holiday gatherings. Guest contributor Veerender Singh Jubbal writes about India's emerging game development scene and how its community is helping elevate local titles to an international stage. Ahead of the launch of Ryu Ga Gatoku’s Stranger Than Heaven, executive editor Brian Shea played a new section of the era-spanning Yakuza/Like a Dragon prequel while picking the brains of its lead designers for details on the game’s plot, themes, and time periods. We also have reviews for Gears of War: E-Day, Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse, Ace Combat 8: Wings of Theve, Control Resonant, Star Wars: Galactic Racer, Silent Hill: Downfall, and many more. Subscribe to Game Informer today to get the Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis cover as your first issue. SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: The Elder Scrolls VI Has An Official Subtitle And It's 'Sentinel'
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary: The headline tells the story: The Elder Scrolls VI has an official subtitle and it's Sentinel. So the full game is now titled The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel, or, as we will undoubtedly refer to it moving forward, as we colloquially do with the previous three games (Morrowind, Oblivion, and Skyrim), Sentinel. The news comes from Bethesda's various social media accounts, which are all sharing the video above. Along with the video, music, and the title, it also shares the text as a quote attributed to Yazar, Moth Priest to High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell (4E 206): "The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate."Sentinel is one of the nine major kingdoms within Hammerfell and is the capital of both the Alik'r Desert region and the Myrkwasa region of the Alik'r (source: elderscrolls.fandom). With this knowledge, it's fair to assume Sentinel will have many desert locations.The name continues the tradition of naming the games after locations in the Elder Scrolls universe. Oblivion is the sort of exception, as it is a realm, but it still counts. We still don't know exactly when The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel will be released, but we're now about seven years from its original announcement at E3 2018.

SteamGlobalNewsA.Title: Yakuza Creator Toshiro Nagoshi's Studio Has Officially Shut Down, Ending Gang Of Dragon's Development With It
SteamGlobalNewsA.Summary: Nagoshi Studio, the developer led by Yakuza/Like a Dragon series creator Toshiro Nagoshi, has officially shut down, ending development of Gang of Dragon, which was revealed at The Game Awards last year. Shareholders resolved to dissolve the studio on October 31, according to a notice published in a Japanese government newspaper called Kanpo, as first reported by Gematsu. This follows a report from Bloomberg earlier this year that said Chinese gaming megacorp NetEase Games was cutting funding to Nagoshi Studio, allowing Nagoshi to seek independent funding elsewhere. It seems he couldn't find funding, and now Nagoshi Studio is no more. NetEase helped Nagoshi found the studio in November 2021. You can watch the Gang of Dragon reveal trailer below for a look at what the team was cooking up:  This closure follows other signals that NetEase is looking to divest from the gaming scene outside of its Chinese studios. A little over a month ago, Suda51's Grasshopper Manufacture left NetEase to go independent again, just months after the launch of Romeo Is A Dead Man. [Source: Kanpo via Gematsu]
